"""S6's output contract: a verdict per finding that can also CORRECT it, plus the batch reducer."""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re
from collections.abc import Callable, Collection
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
from pydantic.json_schema import SkipJsonSchema

from vvaharness.models.scan.findings import Finding
from vvaharness.models.scan._coerce import flag as _coerce_bool
from vvaharness.pipeline.stages.s4.outcomes import InvestigatedFinding, fan_out
from vvaharness.report.cvss import rating as cvss_rating
from vvaharness.report.cvss import score as cvss_score
from vvaharness.rules.cwe import norm_cwe
from vvaharness.util.counters import COUNTERS
from vvaharness.util.json_extract import extract_json

# `"9/10"` / `"9 / 10"`: the prompt's own score notation echoed back.
_OUT_OF_TEN = re.compile(r"\s*([^/]*?)\s*/\s*10\s*")


class VerificationOutcome(BaseModel):
    finding_id: str = Field(description="Echo the FINDING id you were given, verbatim.")
    verdict: Literal["TRUE_POSITIVE", "FALSE_POSITIVE", "INCONCLUSIVE"] = Field(description=
        "TRUE_POSITIVE = the weakness is real and reachable. FALSE_POSITIVE = you read the code "
        "and it does not hold; name the control or fact that refutes it in `reason`. "
        "INCONCLUSIVE = you could not reach the evidence either way. Use it — it is recorded as "
        "undetermined and is the honest answer, where a guessed FALSE_POSITIVE silently deletes "
        "a finding nobody will look at again.")
    confidence: int = Field(ge=0, le=10, description=
        "0-10 on the evidence you actually saw. This is a hard gate: a TRUE_POSITIVE below the "
        "configured floor is dropped as unconfirmed, so do not deflate a finding you confirmed, "
        "and do not inflate one you did not.")

    @field_validator("confidence", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _clamp_confidence(cls, v: object) -> object:
        """Clamp a model-emitted score into 0-10 instead of failing the whole batch; a "N/10" string (the prompt's own scale) reads as N, any other fraction still fails."""
        m = _OUT_OF_TEN.fullmatch(v) if isinstance(v, str) else None
        try:
            f = float(m.group(1) if m else v)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return v
        except OverflowError:
            # float(10**400) overflows where float("1e999") reads inf: same saturation, by sign
            f = math.inf if isinstance(v, int) and v > 0 else -math.inf
        if not math.isfinite(f):
            # int(inf) raises OverflowError the except misses, so 1e999 drops the batch; NaN floors
            score = 10 if f > 0 else 0
        else:
            score = min(10, max(0, int(f)))
        if score != f:
            # Invisible downstream (stderr prints the stored value), so the rewrite is counted here
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_confidence_clamped")
        return score
    reason: str = Field(description="Why, in one or two sentences. Required for every verdict.")
    corrected_cwe: str = Field(default="", description=
        "Set this when the weakness is REAL but the reported CWE is wrong — the id your evidence "
        "actually supports, e.g. the finding says CWE-862 but the missing control is a CSRF token, "
        "so CWE-352. Use it with verdict TRUE_POSITIVE: the defect stands, only its label was off. "
        "Refuting a real weakness because its id was imprecise loses a finding for no reason. "
        "Leave empty when the reported CWE is right.")
    corrected_line_start: int = Field(default=0, description=
        "Set this when the weakness is REAL but reported at the wrong line — the line of the "
        "DANGEROUS STATEMENT ITSELF, never the enclosing def/class/decorator header. Use it "
        "with TRUE_POSITIVE. Leave 0 when the reported line already IS the sink.")
    confirmed_repeat_lines: list[int] = Field(default=[], description=
        "Lines in this same file where you verified the IDENTICAL defect and which are NOT already "
        "one of the findings in this session. The scanner has usually found the repeats it could "
        "see; you are reading the file properly, so this is for the site it missed. Each becomes "
        "its own confirmed finding reusing this one's description, so a site costs one integer. "
        "A line already listed above is ignored — say the ones nobody filed.")
    cvss_vector: str = Field(default="", description=
        "A CVSS 3.1 base vector, e.g. 'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H'. Empty "
        "string if you cannot justify one — never invent metrics to fill it.")
    control_absence: bool = Field(default=False, description=
        "True when this finding describes a missing or absent control — a check, gate, limit or "
        "protection that is not there — rather than a value, privilege, or reachable state an "
        "attacker takes forward. 'No rate limiting on the login route' is an absent control "
        "(true); 'SQL injection returns the password hashes' hands the attacker data (false). "
        "When unsure, leave false.")
    channel: str = Field(default="main", description=
        "'posture' when the finding describes how the artifact is built or deployed — container, "
        "CI, or dependency hygiene — rather than a defect in the application's own code; "
        "otherwise 'main'. 'The container runs as root' is posture; 'the upload handler writes "
        "unsanitised filenames' is main. When unsure, leave 'main'.")
    reframed: bool = Field(default=False, description=
        "Set true ONLY when a reframe duty in the system prompt instructed you to: you refuted "
        "the finding's framing but confirmed the underlying exposure and relabelled it via "
        "corrected_cwe. Leave false otherwise.")

    @field_validator("control_absence", "reframed", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _coerce_flag(cls, v: object) -> bool:
        """Coerce a model-emitted flag to bool, falling back to False rather than failing the batch."""
        return _coerce_bool(v)

    @field_validator("channel", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _coerce_channel(cls, v: object) -> str:
        """Return 'posture' only for exactly that stamp, and the 'main' default for anything else."""
        return "posture" if (isinstance(v, str)
                             and v.strip().lower() == "posture") else "main"
    additional_findings: list[InvestigatedFinding] = Field(default=[], description=
        "DISTINCT weaknesses you noticed in this file while verifying, which the finding above "
        "does not cover. You already have the file open, so reporting one costs almost nothing and "
        "leaving it out means nobody looks at this code again. Same evidence bar as the verdict: "
        "report what you can point at, not what could conceivably be wrong. Empty is fine and "
        "common.")
    # Harness-only, hidden from the model schema; verify_batch overwrites what the model sent
    replayed: SkipJsonSchema[bool] = False


class VerificationOutcomes(BaseModel):
    outcomes: list[VerificationOutcome] = Field(description=
        "ONE entry per FINDING you were given, each echoing that finding's own id. A finding you "
        "omit is recorded as unverified, which drops it — so judge every one, including the ones "
        "you are refuting.")


def _validate_direct(raw: str) -> VerificationOutcomes | None:
    try:
        return VerificationOutcomes.model_validate_json(raw)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _validate_salvaged(raw: str) -> VerificationOutcomes | None:
    try:
        return VerificationOutcomes.model_validate(extract_json(raw))
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _validate_lone(raw: str) -> VerificationOutcomes | None:
    try:
        return VerificationOutcomes(outcomes=[VerificationOutcome.model_validate_json(raw)])
    except ValueError:
        return None


def parse_outcomes(raw: str) -> VerificationOutcomes | None:
    """Parse a reply into outcomes, tolerating JSON-in-prose and a bare single outcome."""
    for attempt in (_validate_direct, _validate_salvaged, _validate_lone):
        parsed = attempt(raw)
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed
    stripped = (raw or "").strip()
    COUNTERS.bump("s6_outcome_truncated" if stripped and not stripped.endswith("}")
                  else "s6_outcome_malformed")
    return None


def split_batch_reply(raw: str, finding_ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, VerificationOutcome]:
    """Fan one batched reply out per finding, dropping ids we never asked about."""
    parsed = parse_outcomes(raw)
    if parsed is None:
        return {}
    wanted = set(finding_ids)
    by_id: dict[str, VerificationOutcome] = {}
    for outcome in parsed.outcomes:
        if outcome.finding_id not in wanted:
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_batch_finding_id_invented")
            continue
        by_id[outcome.finding_id] = outcome
    absent = len(wanted) - len(by_id)
    if absent:
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_batch_finding_omitted", absent)
    return by_id


# `reason` ships to the report, so batching.py's fN ids remap; guards match s8.outcomes._PROSE_ID_RX
_REASON_PROSE_ID_RX = re.compile(r"(?<![\w./$-])f\d+\b(?!\.\w)")


def remap_reason_ids(reason: str, display: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    """Rewrite each batch-local ``fN`` token in *reason* to *display*'s ``file:line``, leaving an unknown id as written."""
    if not reason:
        return reason
    return _REASON_PROSE_ID_RX.sub(
        lambda m: display.get(m.group(0), m.group(0)), reason)


def _corrections(f: Finding, outcome: VerificationOutcome,
                 max_line: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """The verifier's fixes to *f*'s coordinates, bounded by *max_line* (the file's EOF, None when unknown)."""
    fixed: dict = {}
    cwe = norm_cwe(outcome.corrected_cwe)
    if cwe and cwe != f.cwe:
        fixed["cwe"] = cwe
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_cwe_corrected")
    line = outcome.corrected_line_start
    if line > 0 and line != f.line_start:
        # pre_anchor_line is the header s5 moved off (0 if unrun), so a correction back is refused
        if f.pre_anchor_line > 0 and line == f.pre_anchor_line:
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_line_correction_reverted_reanchor")
        elif max_line is not None and line > max_line:
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_line_correction_ignored")
        else:
            fixed["line_start"] = line
            fixed["line_end"] = max(f.line_end, line)
            # s7 must judge the corrected line, not the stale pre-move coordinate.
            fixed["pre_anchor_line"] = 0
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_line_corrected")
    # s5/gates.reject judges only line_start, so this is the only bound on line_end.
    if max_line is not None:
        end = fixed.get("line_end", f.line_end)
        if end > max_line:
            fixed["line_end"] = max_line
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_line_end_clamped_eof")
    return fixed


def _trait_stamps(outcome: VerificationOutcome) -> dict:
    """The verifier's trait stamps, writing only non-default values so a missing stamp keeps the Finding's defaults."""
    stamped: dict = {}
    if outcome.control_absence:
        stamped["control_absence"] = True
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_stamp_control_absence")
    if outcome.channel == "posture":
        stamped["channel"] = "posture"
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_stamp_channel_posture")
    return stamped


def _verdict_fields(outcome: VerificationOutcome) -> dict:
    """The verdict half of the update, with CVSS scored from the vector the verifier gave."""
    # Finding.verdict has no INCONCLUSIVE slot; FALSE_POSITIVE would delete it, so it maps to None
    vector = outcome.cvss_vector.strip() or None
    score = cvss_score(vector) if vector else None
    if outcome.verdict == "TRUE_POSITIVE" and vector and score == 0.0:
        # A real weakness scored zero-impact must not rank last by that 0.0; ship it unscored
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_cvss_zero_impact_on_tp")
        vector, score = None, None
    return {
        "verdict": outcome.verdict if outcome.verdict != "INCONCLUSIVE" else None,
        "verdict_confidence": outcome.confidence,
        "verdict_reason": outcome.reason,
        "cvss_vector": vector,
        "cvss_score": score,
        "cvss_rating": cvss_rating(score) if score is not None else None,
    }


def classify(outcome: VerificationOutcome, min_confidence: int) -> str:
    """The drop bucket this outcome belongs in, so routing reads the verdict, not the Finding."""
    # A tool-free replay is lossy: its low-confidence refutation must not delete the finding unseen
    if (outcome.replayed and outcome.verdict == "FALSE_POSITIVE"
            and outcome.confidence < min_confidence):
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_replayed_fp_held")
        return "INCONCLUSIVE"
    if outcome.verdict == "INCONCLUSIVE":
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_verdict_inconclusive")
        return "INCONCLUSIVE"
    if outcome.verdict == "FALSE_POSITIVE":
        return "FALSE_POSITIVE"
    if outcome.confidence < min_confidence:
        return "UNCONFIRMED"
    return "TRUE_POSITIVE"


def _new_repeat_lines(primary: Finding, outcome: VerificationOutcome,
                      reserve: Callable[[int], bool],
                      max_line: int | None = None) -> list[int]:
    """Confirmed repeat sites that are genuinely new and within *max_line* (EOF, None when unknown)."""
    fresh, stale, oob = [], 0, 0
    for n in sorted(set(outcome.confirmed_repeat_lines)):
        if n <= 0 or n == primary.line_start:
            continue
        if max_line is not None and n > max_line:
            oob += 1
            continue
        # reserve() must check and claim in one step, or two sessions race on the same new line
        if not reserve(n):
            stale += 1
            continue
        fresh.append(n)
    if oob:
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_repeat_beyond_eof", oob)
    if stale:
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_repeat_already_filed", stale)
    if fresh:
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_repeat_confirmed", len(fresh))
    return fresh


def apply_outcome(f: Finding, outcome: VerificationOutcome,
                  reserve: Callable[[int], bool] | None = None, *,
                  stamps: bool = True, reframe: bool = False,
                  max_line: int | None = None,
                  clone_repeats: bool = True) -> list[Finding]:
    """*f* carrying the verdict and any correction, plus one clone per new confirmed repeat site."""
    update = {**_verdict_fields(outcome), **_corrections(f, outcome, max_line)}
    if stamps:
        update.update(_trait_stamps(outcome))
    primary = f.model_copy(update=update)
    if outcome.verdict != "TRUE_POSITIVE":
        return [primary]
    if reserve is None:
        reserve = lambda _line: True
    elif primary.line_start != f.line_start:
        # Claim the corrected line so a sibling's "confirmed repeat" there reads as already filed
        reserve(primary.line_start)
    if reframe and outcome.reframed:
        # A reframed verdict relabels, so it ships alone -- after the claim, so no sibling re-files
        COUNTERS.bump("s6_verdict_reframed")
        return [primary]
    if not clone_repeats:
        if outcome.confirmed_repeat_lines:
            # The re-verify wave owes one verdict each; a clone is a row the ledger misses
            COUNTERS.bump("s6_repeat_clone_reverify_discarded",
                          len(outcome.confirmed_repeat_lines))
        return [primary]
    # A repeat site is a point, not a span copy: a wide span overlaps and dedup collapses the clones
    extra = _new_repeat_lines(primary, outcome, reserve, max_line)
    # Refs/snippet name the PRIMARY's line, so carrying them mis-points; mirrors s4 _at_line
    return [primary, *(primary.model_copy(
                update={"line_start": n, "line_end": n, "is_repeat_clone": True,
                        "code_snippet": "", "sink_ref": None, "source_ref": None,
                        "backfilled_refs": [], "pre_anchor_line": 0})
                       for n in extra)]


def discovered(outcome: VerificationOutcome, parent: Finding, *,
               repo_root: str, inventory: Collection[str]) -> list[Finding]:
    """The weaknesses this session found on its own, fanned out as s4 fans out its own, whatever the parent's verdict."""
    if not outcome.additional_findings:
        return []
    # "+s6"+s6_discovered exclude from the s5 ledger/raw counts/SARIF; no CVSS; clones keep origin
    chunk = f"{parent.chunk_id or 's6'}+s6"
    verdict = {
        "verdict": "TRUE_POSITIVE",
        "verdict_confidence": outcome.confidence,
        "verdict_reason": f"found while verifying {parent.file}:{parent.line_start}",
        "origin": "s6_discovered",
    }
    out: list[Finding] = []
    for extra in outcome.additional_findings:
        out.extend(fan_out(extra, chunk, [parent.cwe] if parent.cwe else [],
                           repo_root=repo_root, inventory=inventory))
    COUNTERS.bump("s6_finding_discovered", len(out))
    return [f.model_copy(update=verdict) for f in out]


def unverified(f: Finding, detail: str) -> Finding:
    """*f* left with no verdict, so a lost reply reads as undetermined rather than clean."""
    return f.model_copy(update={"verdict": None, "verdict_confidence": 0,
                                "verdict_reason": detail})

Use it — it is recorded as undetermined and is the honest answer, where a guessed FALSE_POSITIVE silently deletes a finding nobody will look at again.

0-10 on the evidence you actually saw. This is a hard gate: a TRUE_POSITIVE below the configured floor is dropped as unconfirmed, so do not deflate a finding you confirmed, and do not inflate one you did not.
Why, in one or two sentences. Required for every verdict.

Set this when the weakness is REAL but the reported CWE is wrong — the id your evidence actually supports, e.g. the finding says CWE-862 but the missing control is a CSRF token, so CWE-352. Use it with verdict TRUE_POSITIVE: the defect stands, only its label was off. Refuting a real weakness because its id was imprecise loses a finding for no reason. Leave empty when the reported CWE is right.

Set this when the weakness is REAL but reported at the wrong line — the line of the DANGEROUS STATEMENT ITSELF, never the enclosing def/class/decorator header. Use it with TRUE_POSITIVE. Leave 0 when the reported line already IS the sink.

Lines in this same file where you verified the IDENTICAL defect and which are NOT already one of the findings in this session. The scanner has usually found the repeats it could see; you are reading the file properly, so this is for the site it missed. Each becomes its own confirmed finding reusing this one's description, so a site costs one integer. A line already listed above is ignored — say the ones nobody filed.

True when this finding describes a missing or absent control — a check, gate, limit or protection that is not there — rather than a value, privilege, or reachable state an attacker takes forward. 'No rate limiting on the login route' is an absent control (true); 'SQL injection returns the password hashes' hands the attacker data (false). When unsure, leave false.

'posture' when the finding describes how the artifact is built or deployed — container, CI, or dependency hygiene — rather than a defect in the application's own code; otherwise 'main'. 'The container runs as root' is posture; 'the upload handler writes unsanitised filenames' is main. When unsure, leave 'main'.

Set true ONLY when a reframe duty in the system prompt instructed you to: you refuted the finding's framing but confirmed the underlying exposure and relabelled it via corrected_cwe. Leave false otherwise.

You already have the file open, so reporting one costs almost nothing and leaving it out means nobody looks at this code again. Same evidence bar as the verdict: report what you can point at, not what could conceivably be wrong. Empty is fine and common.
ONE entry per FINDING you were given, each echoing that finding's own id. A finding you omit is recorded as unverified, which drops it — so judge every one, including the ones you are refuting.
